Weigh the continue / bluff-catch read against the REALIZED figure, not the raw one — but this is heuristic context: a decisive pot-odds price FACT and the hard equity FACT above still take precedence.]

[HEURISTIC — SPR & COMMITMENT (effective stack ÷ pot, hero-centric; ESTIMATED, not exact): flop SPR ~12.1 — to get all-in profitably needs ~48% equity (high SPR — favours pot control with one-pair hands); turn SPR ~6.2 — to get all-in profitably needs ~46% equity (high SPR — favours pot control with one-pair hands). Use this for the call-vs-raise / stack-off decision, NOT the bluff-catch call (pot odds govern that): at low SPR a strong-enough made hand should commit, at high SPR a one-pair hand favours pot control. With a marginal made hand villain's stack-off range skews to sets/two-pair, so require more than the raw %. The stack-off % is the equity to get all-in profitably versus a willing range, NOT hero's pot-odds price. This is heuristic context — a decisive pot-odds price FACT and the hard equity FACT still take precedence.]
